passage:
Mason's backpack broke on the way to school. Books fell onto the sidewalk, and papers flew everywhere.
Two students he did not know stopped to help. One picked up notebooks. The other gave him a plastic bag for loose papers.
Mason thanked them, but he forgot to ask their names.
At school, he told his teacher what happened. The teacher suggested writing a thank-you note and putting it on the hallway board.
The next day, one of the students saw the note and smiled.
Mason learned that thanks can still be given even when you do not know exactly who helped you. A public thank-you may reach the right person in the end.
